@@ -0,0 +1,4 @@ +

The Vote delegated log call holds no wallet address — KS-2173, governance, TIER 2

+
What to know. delegateVote in services/governance/src/services/governanceService.ts now logs Vote delegated with { delegationId } alone (before: the delegation id plus both wallet addresses). The delegation record in the database still keeps both addresses. Cells: services/governance/src/__tests__/ks2173-vote-delegated-log-holds-no-wallet-address.test.ts, run with the governance jest runner (npm --prefix Blockchain/Dev/services/governance test). +
Not changed: the request log and the shared errorHandler (KS-2173 part 2). A log search for a wallet address after a delegation should now find nothing from this call; the live log was not read. +

@@ -0,0 +1,18 @@ +

. The Vote delegated log call no longer writes either wallet address (KS-2173, governance, TIER 2)

+
What this changes. Before, delegateVote in Blockchain/Dev/services/governance/src/services/governanceService.ts logged Vote delegated with { delegationId, delegatorAddress, delegateAddress }, so every delegation wrote both wallet addresses into the governance service log. A wallet address is the data subject's own data (KS-1955). +
Now the call logs { delegationId: delegation.id } alone. Wednesday's ruling: no other id is added, because whether a participant id is personal data is not measured. One comment line above the call says why and cites KS-2173. Nothing else in the function changes: the delegation record still keeps both addresses and the response is the same. +
The new cell file Blockchain/Dev/services/governance/src/__tests__/ks2173-vote-delegated-log-holds-no-wallet-address.test.ts runs the real delegateVote over a small ../db dispatcher (two participant reads, one empty active-delegations read, one delegation save; any other statement is refused) and a logger that records every call at every level. Its two controls pass before and after the fix: the log call is reached exactly once (so the other cells cannot pass vacuously) and the record keeps both addresses. Its two test cells fail against the unchanged code: the meta holds neither wallet string, and the meta is the delegation id alone with no wallet string in any logged call. +
+

.1 Evidence

+
How it was checked. Run in a clean worktree on develop bba80c3c8e24, with the governance jest runner (Node v26.8.1): +
    +
  • cell file against the unchanged product file: 4 tests, 2 failed (the two test cells), 2 passed (the two controls);
    • +
  • against the fix: 4 passed;
    • +
  • the call planted back with delegatorAddress: delegator.walletAddress: the same 2 cells fail again, and the file was restored byte for byte afterwards;
    • +
  • whole services/governance suite: 20 suites and 367 tests before, 21 suites and 371 tests after, all passing.
    • +
+
The governance runner was first proved on an existing cell (the KS-1940 file, 24 tests passing) before any number above was relied on. +
+

.2 What it does not cover

+
Not measured here. Any live log (production's log level and log store are unmeasured). The other two layers KS-2173 names, the request log Request received in the governance index.ts and the shared errorHandler in packages/shared, are part 2 and are not changed. Nothing was run on Node 24. The open PR for KS-2060 edits the same file in other places; that overlap is measured in this PR's body, not here. +
